panel.cryptoHeroText: Your viewers donate with Tether (USDT) from anywhere in the world, and the money goes *straight to your own wallet*. No middleman in between.
panel.cryptoFeatPage: A donation page of your own, with your name
panel.cryptoFeatWallet: Wallet to wallet: Jarchi never holds any money
panel.cryptoRejected: Your request wasn't approved. You can request again in {time}.
panel.cryptoLost: This Jarchi's gateway was approved, but its key can't be read on this PC any more. Request it again.
panel.cryptoAskSub: The request is for your own channel: you'll sign in with it in your browser to show it's yours.
cryptoTerms: Sending a request *does not mean you will get the gateway*.
Approving or rejecting a request is entirely up to *Jarchi's policies*, and a request may be rejected without a reason.
Jarchi never receives or holds any money. Donations go straight to your own wallet, and *you are responsible for your wallet addresses being correct*.
Jarchi may *turn the gateway off, for a while or for good*, whenever it sees fit, for example if it is misused.
The answer to your request shows up here in Jarchi.
panel.cryptoAgree: I've read the terms above and accept them.
panel.cryptoSentText: Jarchi Pay opened in your browser. Sign in there with your channel's Kick or Twitch account to send the request. The answer shows up right here.
panel.cryptoNoChannelText: To request the crypto gateway, connect your Kick or Twitch channel to Jarchi.
panel.cryptoToastText: There are a few important things you need to read
panel.cryptoHelloText: Before you start, read these few points carefully.
cryptoHelloRules: The money goes straight to your own wallet
Jarchi never holds the money and has no access to it. It only checks that a donation came in, so it can play the alert.
Copy the address from your wallet itself and check it once more. If the address is wrong, money sent to it never comes back, and Jarchi can't do anything about it.
Each network has its own address
Don't put a `BEP20` address in place of a `TRC20` one, or the other way round.
Changing an address later takes 24 hours
The first time, your addresses are saved right away. But for safety, any change after that waits 24 hours, and you can cancel it during that time.
Once your addresses are saved, your donation page is here: `{page}`. Put its link in your bio and your channel panels.

Before you give the link to your viewers, send a $1 donation yourself. The money comes back to your own wallet, minus just the network fee (very low on BEP20). That way you know the address is right and the alert plays.

Open a ticket on Jarchi's Support page. Viewers can also send a message from the donation page itself. But remember: Jarchi only **tracks** donations and **can't return** any money. If the wallet address is wrong, the wrong network is picked, or anything else like that, the money is lost.
panel.cryptoHelloRead: Read to the end to be able to tick the box
panel.cryptoHelloAgree: I've read all of these points and I agree
cryptoTourSteps: Copy each network's address from your wallet itself and put it here. Until an address is saved, your donation page won't open.
Pick one of the ready-made designs or make your own alert. You can also set separate alerts for bigger donations.
Crypto alerts play in the same Alerts link you already have in OBS, so there's no new link to add. Play a test alert to make sure it works.
Your donation page's picture, banner and bio are here. You can also make a ready-made banner for your Kick and Twitch channel panels.
Every donation that comes in shows up here with its name and message. With “Pop out” you can also open it next to your game.

groups.alerts: Click an alert to edit it. Its switch turns it on or off. Alerts play for both Kick and Twitch; a logo means it's for that platform only.
groups.goals: Kick's goals and Twitch's goals, each on its own tab with its sync switch. Click a goal to edit it. Its switch only hides it on stream: it keeps counting.

theme.main: The look every alert uses, unless an alert has its own theme. Hover a card to preview it, click it to use it.

appearance.palette: The panel's colors: backgrounds, cards and the main color. **System** uses your Windows accent color (Jarchi's colors if it can't be read). Point at a card to see the whole panel in it; click it to keep it. The small gold details stay gold in every theme. Dark or Light: the moon and sun in the top bar. Only this panel changes, in this browser.
appearance.textSize: Makes the whole panel bigger or smaller: text, buttons and spacing. Only this panel changes, in this browser.
appearance.bgArt: Faint, blurred icons float behind the panel and slowly drift out of the mouse's way. With a Kick or Twitch channel set (Chat page), your own profile pictures float there too, with a ring in the platform's color. The sidebar, top bar and cards become a little see-through. Turn it off for a plain background. Only this panel changes, in this browser.
appearance.reduceMotion: Stops the background art moving: the icons and pictures stay where they are instead of drifting and moving out of the mouse's way. Less work for your PC and its graphics card while you stream or play. The art also stays still when Windows' animation effects are off (**Settings → Accessibility → Visual effects**). Only this panel changes, in this browser.
appearance.language: The panel's language. The page reloads and comes back here. The text of your widgets in OBS doesn't change.

alert.look: **Kick gift** shows Kick's own picture of the gift with Kick-style text. **Use theme** shows it like the other alerts.
alert.theme: A theme for this alert only. Keep "Same as main" to follow the main theme.
alert.media: Your own image, GIF or video instead of the theme's animation: upload a file or paste a link (a Giphy or Tenor page works too; Jarchi downloads it once). It always fits the alert's picture area, whatever its size. Max 10 MB; bigger images and GIFs are made 512 px, still animated. Only WebM keeps a transparent background.
alert.sound: **Theme default** plays the theme's sound, **My sound** a file you upload, **No sound** nothing.
alert.template: The text on screen. `{user}` becomes the viewer's name, `{amount}` the amount, `{months}` the months, `{platform}` Kick or Twitch.
alert.tiers: A different image and sound for bigger amounts. Example: one GIF for 100 Kicks, another for 1,000.
alert.frame: The box around the alert: the theme's, your own colors, or none.
alert.frameOpacity: How solid the frame is. 0% is see-through.
alert.frameRadius: How round the frame's corners are.
alert.textPos: Where the text goes: above, below, or on top of the image.
alert.textAlign: Lines the text up on the left, in the center or on the right.
alert.fontSize: **Auto** (the default): the biggest size that fits the alert, so the text is always readable. **Custom**: your own size; text that wouldn't fit still gets smaller.
alert.textStyle: How the alert's text looks. The viewer's name and the message (the rest of the text) each have their own color, font, bold and outline/shadow; the size is one for the whole line. **Theme** leaves it to the alert's theme. The preview shows every change; **Reset** brings the theme's look back.
alert.bold: On: bold, as the theme draws it (or bold in a font you picked). Off: regular letters.
alert.nameColor: Color of the viewer's name. **Theme** uses the theme's color, **Custom** your own.
alert.textColor: Color of the message: the rest of the text and the viewer's message under it. Numbers keep the theme's highlight color. **Theme** uses the theme's color, **Custom** your own.
alert.font: The typeface of the name or of the message. Each of these has Persian and English letters. **Theme's font** keeps the theme's own.
alert.textShadow: The theme's outline or shadow around the name's or the message's letters, which keeps them readable over a busy game. Off: plain letters.
alert.size: How much of the Browser Source box this alert fills. At 100% it fills the whole box; lower makes it smaller without touching OBS. **Apply to all alerts** gives every alert this size. To move it or make it bigger, drag and resize the box in OBS. Nothing is ever cut off.
alert.duration: How many seconds the alert stays on screen. Bigger amounts add a little more.
alert.volume: How loud this alert's sound (and video) plays.
alert.minAmount: Smaller amounts don't play an alert; goals still count them. Example: 10 keeps single Kicks out.
alert.videoSound: For a video: muted, only the video's own sound, or the video plus the alert sound.
alert.customCss: Your own CSS on top of this alert's look, in the preview and in OBS (CSS only). Main classes: `.alert` (the whole alert, with `.type-sub`, `.tier-2`, `.plat-kick`…), `.media` (picture or emblem), `.box` (text box), `.text` (the words), `.hl` (name and numbers), `.msg` (the viewer's message), `.badge`, `.fx` (effects). Kicks in Kick's look: `.kick-alert`, `.kick-text`. A rule that doesn't take may need `!important`.

goal.title: The text viewers see with the goal, for example "Subs".
goal.target: The number to reach. When it's reached, the goal turns the "full" color and celebrates.
goal.current: The count right now. **−** and **+** change it by one step, or type a number. It's kept when Jarchi restarts.
goal.style: A ready-made look to start from. Every option below works with every style.
goal.textColor: Color of the title and numbers.
goal.fullColor: The bar's color once the target is reached.
goal.bg: **Color**: a box behind the goal. **Transparent**: a box without fill. **Off**: no box.
goal.bgOpacity: How solid the box is. 0% is see-through.
goal.radius: How round the corners of the box and the bar are.
goal.scale: How much of the Browser Source box the goal fills. At 100% it fills the box; to move it or make it bigger, drag and resize the box in OBS.
goal.fontSize: **Auto** (the default): the biggest size that fits, so the title and numbers are always readable. **Custom**: your own size; text that wouldn't fit still gets smaller.
goal.font: The typeface of the goal's text.
goal.titlePos: The title above or below the bar, inside it, or hidden.
goal.showPercent: Shows how far along it is, for example 64%.
goal.showNumbers: Shows the count and the target, for example 32 / 50.
goal.celebrate: Confetti and a glow, once, when the target is reached.
goal.kickSync: Goals you set on your Kick channel (Kick's creator dashboard: followers, subscriptions, KICKs) show Kick's own count and target, here and on stream: read every minute, and at once when Kick sends a change. A goal with nothing set on Kick stays as you set it here. If Kick can't be reached, the last numbers stay.
goal.twitchSync: Goals you set on your Twitch channel (Twitch's Creator Dashboard: followers, subs, bits) show Twitch's own count and target, here and on stream, as Twitch sends them. It needs your Twitch account connected on **Connections**. A goal with nothing set on Twitch stays as you set it here.
goal.celebrateSound: The celebration's sound: the theme's, your own file, or none.
goal.volume: How loud the celebration sound plays.
goal.customCss: Your own CSS on top of this goal's look, in the preview and in OBS (CSS only). Main classes: `.goal` (the whole goal, with `.style-classic`… and `.full` once reached), `.label`, `.title`, `.nums` (count / target), `.pct` (percent), `.track` and `.fill` (the bar), `.ring` and `.ring-pct` (Circle), `.blocks` (Retro). A rule that doesn't take may need `!important`.

viewers.links: One link per count: Kick's, Twitch's, or Total (both added up). Each needs that account connected on the Connections page.
viewers.style: A ready-made look to start from. Picking a style (again) brings back its own font and colors.
viewers.icon: Jarchi gold's icon: People, the Kick or Twitch logo, or **Switch**: the people icon and the platform's logo take turns every few seconds (Total: both logos).
viewers.chartMinutes: Live chart: how far back its line goes.
viewers.offline: While you're not live (or that account isn't connected): **Show "Offline"** in its place, or **Hide** the widget.
viewers.anim: How the number changes. **Roll**, **Flip** and **Fade** move only the digits that changed; **Pop** bounces the whole number.
viewers.size: How much of the Browser Source box it fills. At 100% it fills the box; to move it or make it bigger, drag and resize the box in OBS.
viewers.numberColor: Color of the number (and Jarchi gold's people icon, Comic's eye).
viewers.bgColor: The card's, bar's or bubble's fill.
viewers.accentColor: Jarchi gold's border, Live chart's line, Comic's border and shadow.
viewers.customCss: Your own CSS on top of this widget's look, in the preview and in OBS (CSS only). Main classes: `.viewers` (the whole widget, with `.style-gold`…, `.src-kick` / `.src-twitch` / `.src-total` and `.offline`), `.num` (the number), `.card`, `.icon`, `.chart`, `.block` and `.bar` (Angled bar), `.bubble` (Comic). A rule that doesn't take may need `!important`.

chat.kickChannel: Your channel name, as in `kick.com/name`. Brings the chat and real Kick alerts. No login.
chat.twitchChannel: Your channel name, as in `twitch.tv/name`. Brings the chat and real Twitch alerts. No login.
chat.style: A ready-made look to start from. Every option in the tabs works with every style.
chat.showPlatform: A small Kick or Twitch logo before each name.
chat.showBadges: Badges before names, like mod, VIP or sub.
chat.badgeOther: Every other badge, for example OG, founder or sub gifter.
chat.badgeMode: **Important only**: broadcaster, mod, VIP, OG, founder, sub, Kick's sub gifter, verified and staff. **All**: every badge, Twitch's gifter tiers and levels too.
chat.badgeSize: How big badges are next to the name. 100% is as tall as the name.
chat.badgeBg: A small dark square behind Kick's and Twitch's own badges (OG, mod, VIP, verified, founder, broadcaster, staff, sub gifter), which are made for dark chats. **Auto**: only where the message background is light. **Always**: on every message. **Off**: never. Sub badges never get one.
chat.ogHat: Kick viewers with the OG badge get a black hat with MP on it.
chat.hatStyle: The hat: a cap, a beanie or a fedora.
chat.hatPos: **First letter** / **Last letter**: on the name. **Badge**: a small hat with the badges, instead of the OG badge. **Profile picture**: on the picture (with profile pictures off: on the first letter).
chat.showTime: The time each message was sent.
chat.showColon: A colon between the name and the message.
chat.replies: When a viewer replies to another message. **Small line above**: "↩ replying to name: start of their message…" above the reply. **Name only**: "@name" before it. **Quote box**: their message in a small faded box above it. **Hidden**: the message as usual, without who it answers. The same in every style.
chat.emotesKick: Kick emotes as pictures. Off: their names show as text.
chat.emotesTwitch: Twitch emotes as pictures. Off: their names show as text.
chat.emotes7tv: 7TV emotes (the channel's and the global ones) as pictures.
chat.emotesAnimated: Animated emotes move. Off: they stand still.
chat.bigEmotes: A message with only emotes shows them bigger.
chat.nameColorMode: **Platform color**: each name's own color from Kick or Twitch. **Style colors**: the style's. **One color**: the same for everyone.
chat.readableNames: A platform color that is hard to read on the box (light on light, dark on dark) gets just enough lighter or darker to read well. It stays the same color.
chat.namePos: The name on the same line as the message, or above it.
chat.textShadow: A soft shadow that keeps text readable on busy backgrounds.
chat.textDir: **Auto** puts Persian and Arabic messages right to left, everything else left to right.
chat.bg: **Color**: a box behind the chat. **Transparent**: a box without fill. **Off**: no box.
chat.bgOpacity: How solid the box is. 0% is see-through.
chat.bubbles: Each message in its own bubble instead of one big box.
chat.borderColorMode: **User's color**: each message's border takes the sender's name color from Kick or Twitch; someone without one gets the Border color above. **Custom**: the Border color above for every message. Shown when each message has its own border (bubbles, or Background Off).
chat.padding: Space inside the box, around the messages.
chat.width: Width of the chat. Make the OBS source at least this wide.
chat.height: Height of the chat here in the preview. In OBS a chat (not a bar) is as tall as its source: a taller source shows more messages.
chat.layout: **Vertical**: a list of messages. **Horizontal**: one bar where messages scroll by.
chat.tickerDir: Which way messages move along the bar.
chat.tickerSpeed: How fast the bar moves, in pixels per second.
chat.tickerLoop: When chat is quiet, the bar keeps showing the last messages again.
chat.tickerPos: Puts the bar at the top or the bottom of a taller OBS source.
chat.maxMessages: How many messages stay on screen; older ones leave.
chat.hideAfter: Each message leaves after this many seconds. 0 = never.
chat.enterAnim: How a new message comes in.
chat.animSpeed: Faster or slower animations. ×2 is twice as fast.
chat.fade: Old messages fade out softly at the edge instead of being cut off.
chat.fadeZone: How big that soft edge is.
chat.typewriter: The newest message is typed out letter by letter.
chat.typeSound: A soft typing sound while it types.
chat.hideCommands: Hides messages that start with `!`, like `!discord`.
chat.hideBots: Hides messages from the names in **Bots**.
chat.bots: Bot names to hide, separated by commas.
chat.hiddenUsers: Viewers whose messages never show, separated by commas.
chat.blockedWords: A message with any of these words is hidden. Separate them with commas.
chat.hideLinks: Hides messages that contain a link.
chat.source: Both chats, only Kick, or only Twitch.
chat.fxSubGlow: Sub lines glow gold, with a SUBSCRIBER tag. While special sub lines are on (above), a sub gets that line instead: this is for the other sub lines, like the viewers a gift went to.
chat.fxFirst: A viewer's very first message in your chat gets a sparkly tag.
chat.fxRainbowVip: VIPs' names shine in rainbow colors.
chat.rainbowUsers: More names that get the rainbow, separated by commas.
chat.fxMention: Messages that mention your channel name stand out.
chat.fxCombo: When people send the same emote again and again, it shows once with a counter (x12).
chat.avatars: Profile pictures next to names. Kick: real pictures, or Kick's own default picture for viewers without one. Twitch: real pictures too (no key needed), or the first letter of the name when one can't be found.
chat.blur: Blurs what's behind a see-through box, like frosted glass.
chat.showTiming: For finding chat delays. Each new message gets a small label like `+1.2s`: how long after Kick or Twitch made it, it showed here, with this PC's clock error taken off. The window where Jarchi runs prints one line per message with each step: **received** (Jarchi got it), **sent** (to the chat), **shown** (the chat drew it). Turn it off when you're done.
chat.enabled: Off: the chat is hidden on stream. Kick and Twitch stay connected, so alerts still come.
chat.eventKicks: A special line when someone sends Kicks, with Kick's gift picture, its name and what it's worth: **LifeWing sent HELL YEAH ×1 · 1 Kicks**, then their message.
chat.eventKicksMin: Gifts worth fewer Kicks than this get no line. 0 = every gift.
chat.eventSubs: Subs and resubs as a special line: **Ali subscribed for 6 months!**, then their message. Off: the usual sub line.
chat.eventGifts: Gifted subs as a special line: **Rich gifted 5 subs!** Off: the usual line.
chat.eventGiftsMin: Gifts of fewer subs than this keep the usual line. 0 = every gift.
chat.eventBits: A cheer as a special line, with Twitch's gem for the amount: **Sara cheered 500 bits!**, then the message. Off: the usual message.
chat.eventBitsMin: Cheers of fewer bits than this stay a usual message. 0 = every cheer.
chat.eventRaids: A special line when a channel raids you (on Kick: hosts you), with how many viewers came.
chat.eventLook: **Card**: a tinted card with a bar in Kick's green or Twitch's purple. **Glow**: a glowing ring. **Simple line**: just the words. Each works inside every chat style.
chat.eventLonger: Special lines stay on screen twice as long: twice the **Hide each message after** time, and until twice **Max messages on screen** newer ones came. In a bar they go by twice.
chat.customCss: Your own CSS on top of this chat's look, in the preview and in OBS (CSS only). Main classes: `.chat` (the whole chat, with `.style-kick`…), `.msg` (each message; `.event` for special lines), `.meta` (the start of the line), `.name`, `.badges` and `.badge`, `.platform`, `.avatar`, `time`, `.body` (the words), `.emote`, `.reply`. A rule that doesn't take may need `!important`.

settings.showBadge: A small Kick or Twitch badge on alerts. It only shows when both accounts are connected.
settings.testAs: Which platform test alerts come from. `{platform}` in the alert text shows its name.
settings.alertGap: Seconds of quiet between two alerts.
settings.proxyMode: **Off** (the default): always directly; Jarchi never turns a proxy on by itself. **Windows proxy**: the proxy Windows is set to (VPN apps often set it). **Manual**: a proxy you type in, or the VPN app you said Yes to. Only Jarchi's own connections use it; Jarchi never changes Windows' proxy setting.
settings.proxyType: Your VPN or proxy app tells you which. v2rayN: SOCKS5 on `10808`, HTTP on `10809`.
settings.proxyHost: The proxy's address. For a VPN app on this PC: `127.0.0.1`.
settings.obsUrl: The alerts link for OBS. Add it as a Browser Source, 800 × 600, then drag the box where you want the alerts.
settings.reset: Deletes every change and every uploaded file. Click twice to confirm.

start.title: Getting started
start.intro: Jarchi runs on your own PC and shows alerts, a chat box and goals in OBS. No account and no login: your Kick and Twitch channel names are enough for real alerts.
steps: Keep Jarchi running
Start Jarchi and leave its window open while you stream. This panel is at `{panelUrl}`.
Type your channel names
Open **Chat** in the menu and type your Kick and/or Twitch channel. Each name also brings that platform's real alerts.
Pick a theme
Open **Alerts** and click **Theme** at the top. Every alert uses it, unless you give an alert its own.
Add Jarchi to OBS
Add the alerts to OBS as a Browser Source. The next topic shows how.
Test it
In **Alerts**, pick an alert in the list and press **Test in OBS**. It plays in OBS and shows up in the alert queue.
start.tip: Start Jarchi before OBS. If OBS was open first, right-click the Jarchi source in OBS and choose **Refresh**.

obs.title: Add Jarchi to OBS
obs.intro: Every part of Jarchi is a web page that OBS shows as a Browser Source. The alerts, the chat and each goal have their own link.
steps: Copy the link

On the **Alerts** page, click **Copy link: all alerts**. The alerts link is `{alertsUrl}`. An alert's own **Copy link** (next to **Test in OBS**) plays only that alert; while it's open in OBS, the main link skips it.
Add a Browser Source
In OBS: **Sources → + → Browser**. Give it a name, for example "Jarchi Alerts".
Paste it and set the size
Paste the link into **URL**. Width **800**, height **600**.
Turn on the sound
Tick **Control audio via OBS**, so alert sounds go through the OBS mixer to your stream. Then click **OK**.
Place it

In the OBS preview, drag the box to where the alerts should show and pull its corners to make it bigger or smaller. The alert always fills the box, picture and text together, so what you see is what plays. **Alert size** in each alert's **Style** tab makes it smaller inside the box.
Chat and goals
The same steps, with their own link and size. Chat: `{chatUrl}`, 420 × 600. Goals: `{goalSubsUrl}` and `{goalKicksUrl}`, 800 × 200 (Circle style: 400 × 400); a goal fills its box too.
obs.tip: Jarchi must be running when OBS loads the source. If you started OBS first, right-click the source and choose **Refresh**. After that it reconnects by itself whenever Jarchi restarts.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.intro: Seven alerts: follow, sub, resub, gifted subs, Kicks, bits and raid. Each has its own picture, sound and text.
steps: Pick an alert
Click it in the **Alerts** list. The switch next to it turns it on or off; the Kick and Twitch logos show where it comes from.
Preview it

The preview plays the alert exactly as OBS will, and again after every change. **Replay** plays it once more, **Dark**, **Light** and **Checkered** change only the preview's background, and **Test in OBS** sends it to OBS.
Media, Sound, Text, Style

The four tabs under the preview. **Media**: your own image, GIF or video (or the theme's), how long it stays, the minimum amount. **Sound**: the theme's, your own or none, the volume, a video's sound. **Text**: the words (`{user}` `{amount}` `{months}` `{platform}` become the real values), position, size and color. **Style**: a theme for this alert only, and the frame.
Different media by amount
In **Media**, Kicks, gifted subs and bits can play their own picture and sound for bigger amounts. Turn it on and upload per amount.
No Save button
Every change saves by itself, text a moment after you stop typing. A small **Saved** at the bottom of the page says it's done.
alerts.tip: Real Kick alerts (subs, resubs, gifted subs, Kicks and hosts) come from your Kick channel name in **Chat**, with no login. Real Twitch alerts (subs, resubs, gifted subs, raids and bits) come from your Twitch channel name the same way. Follows come once your Kick and Twitch accounts are connected on **Connections**. The **Test** buttons work for every alert.

goals.title: Goals
goals.intro: Six goals on two tabs. **Kick**: a Sub goal (subs, resubs and gifted subs), a Kicks goal and a Followers goal. **Twitch**: a Sub goal, a Bits goal and a Followers goal. Each one counts its own platform's events by itself, never the other's. With **Sync from Kick** or **Sync from Twitch** (at the top of each tab), a goal you also set on that channel shows that channel's own numbers.
steps: Open a goal
Open **Goals** and click a goal on the **Kick** or **Twitch** tab.
Title and target
Type the title viewers see and the number to reach.
Fix the count
In the list, click a goal's number and type another one, or press **Reset to 0** (twice) for a new goal. In the editor, **−** and **+** change it by one step. The count is kept when Jarchi restarts.
Pick a look
Choose a style, then change colors, box, font and size in **More options**. **Reset style** brings the style's own look back.
Add it to OBS
Click **Copy OBS link** and add it as a Browser Source, 800 × 200 (Circle style: 400 × 400). The goal fills the box: drag and resize it in OBS.
goals.tip: When the target is reached, the bar turns the "full" color and celebrates once. The switch in the list only hides the goal on stream; it keeps counting.

viewers.title: Viewer count
viewers.intro: How many people watch you right now, on your stream: Kick's count, Twitch's, or both added up (**Total**). Jarchi reads them from the Kick and Twitch accounts connected on **Connections**, about every 30 seconds while you're live.
steps: Connect your accounts
On **Connections**, connect Kick, Twitch or both. The **Viewer count** page says which one isn't connected yet.
Pick a look
Open **Viewer count** and choose a style, then the font, size, colors and how the number changes. Press **Test** to see it change in the preview.
Add it to OBS
Under **OBS links**, click **Copy OBS link** for Kick, Twitch or Total and add it as a Browser Source, 400 × 200. It fills the box: drag and resize it in OBS.
viewers.tip: Not live? It shows "Offline", or nothing at all with **Hide** under **When not live**. While you're live, the number updates about every 30 seconds.

chat.title: Chat widget
chat.intro: Kick and Twitch chat together in one box on your stream, with Kick, Twitch and 7TV emotes.
steps: Type your channels
On the **Chat** page, type your Kick and/or Twitch channel name. No login. Each one says **Connected** when it works.
Pick a style
18 vertical styles and 9 horizontal bars (**Vertical** / **Horizontal** above them). A style is a starting point: every option works with every style.
Try it
**Send test message** (the arrow next to it: **Send 10 messages**, **Show all effects**) fills the preview and OBS with sample messages. **Replay** plays the last ones again in the preview.
Fine-tune it
The tabs: **Text**, **Names & badges**, **Events** (special lines for Kicks, subs, gift subs, bits and raids), **Filters** and **Layout** (size, box and motion).
Add it to OBS
Click **Copy OBS link** and add it as a Browser Source, 420 × 600. Make it at least as big as the chat's width and height; the horizontal bars need width 1920.
chat.tip: The **Show the chat on stream** switch (under the preview) only hides the chat on stream. Real Kick and Twitch alerts keep coming either way.

queue.title: Alert queue
queue.intro: Alerts play one after another, never on top of each other. The **Alert queue** page shows what's playing and what's waiting.
steps: Now playing
The alert on screen, with a bar for the time it has left.
Pause, Skip, Clear
**Pause** lets the current alert finish and holds the rest. **Skip** ends the current one. **Clear queue** (click twice) removes everything waiting.
Waiting and Replay
× takes one waiting alert out. **Last played** keeps the last 10, each with **Replay**.
Gap between alerts
In **Settings**, choose how many seconds pass between two alerts.
queue.tip: If OBS is closed, alerts wait and play when it opens again; the page says so at the top. In the menu, the number next to **Alert queue** is how many alerts are waiting.

proxy.title: Proxy & VPN
proxy.intro: If Kick, Twitch or 7TV is filtered where you are, Jarchi can connect through your own VPN app. Only Jarchi's connections go through it (chat pictures too), never the rest of your PC. Jarchi never uses public proxies.
steps: It finds your VPN app

When Kick, Twitch or Jarchi's server can't be reached, Jarchi looks for a VPN app running on this PC (v2rayN, NekoBox, Hiddify, Clash, Karing…) and tests it. If one works, it asks: **VPN found: … Use it for Jarchi?** Nothing changes until you choose **Yes**, which sets Jarchi's proxy to **Manual** with it.
Open the setting
**Connections → Proxy**. **Off** (the default) connects directly; **Windows proxy** uses the proxy Windows is set to; **Look for VPN apps** looks now. Jarchi never changes Windows' own proxy setting.
Manual

If nothing is found, pick HTTP or SOCKS5 and type your VPN app's local address and port, for example `127.0.0.1` and `10808` (SOCKS5 in v2rayN). The port is in your VPN app's settings, often called Local port, SOCKS port, HTTP port or Mixed port.
Test it
**Test connection** checks Kick, Twitch and 7TV and says in plain words what works. The dot next to **Proxy** shows the result.
proxy.tip: If the proxy stops working (say, your VPN app was closed), a warning shows at the top: click it to look again. If your VPN runs in TUN mode (the whole PC goes through it), **Off** works too. Proxies with a username and password, and PAC scripts, aren't supported.

fix.title: If something doesn't work
fix.intro: Click a question to see what to check.

faq.q: The alert doesn't show in OBS
a: Is Jarchi running? Start it before OBS, or right-click the source in OBS and choose **Refresh**.
If the **Alert queue** page says the OBS overlay isn't open, OBS hasn't loaded the page. Check that the URL is exactly `{alertsUrl}`.
The source should be visible and in the scene you're live on. The alert fills its box: if the box is tiny in the OBS preview, pull its corners.
Is the alert switched on in the list? Is the queue paused? Kicks below the **Minimum amount** (10 by default) don't play.
In the source's properties in OBS, tick **Control audio via OBS**, then check that the source isn't muted in the OBS mixer.
Check that the alert's **Sound** isn't **No sound**, and its **Volume** in the **Sound** tab.
The **Sound** box under the preview only mutes the preview here in the panel.
For a video with its own sound, choose **Video sound** in the **Sound** tab.

faq.q: Kick won't connect, or it's filtered
a: **channel not found**: type the name exactly as in your Kick link, `kick.com/name`.

**blocked** or **can't reach it**: Kick is filtered or blocked on your network. Turn on your VPN app: Jarchi offers to connect through it. Or set it up in **Connections → Proxy** and press **Test connection**.
Jarchi keeps retrying by itself; there's no need to restart it.
Does the channel say **Connected** under **Chat**? Is the chat switched on?
Send a test message. If it shows here but not in OBS, refresh the source in OBS and make it at least as big as the chat (420 × 600 is enough for the default style).
Check the filters: **Show from**, **Hidden users**, **Blocked words** and **Hide each message after**.

faq.q: Alerts are late or pile up
a: Alerts play one at a time, so a burst waits in line. Lower **Duration** or **Gap between alerts**, or use **Skip** and **Clear queue**.
Raise the Kicks alert's **Minimum amount** to keep small taps out of the line (goals still count them).
Kick sends some events a few seconds late, and an automatic resub waits about 10 seconds for its months. That's normal.
